thread:
maya: deploy-bot quarantined canary in eu-west for invoices-svc after chart v4.0.1. sudden DB connection surge and elevated latency.
deploy-bot: [automated] Canary health check: 6/8 pods > 400 DB conns; p95 latency +700ms; recommend quarantine + hold promotion.
owen: quick diff shows values bump: db.pool.max: 60 -> 450 (accidental). That explains the flood. Change window ends in ~35m.
sre-oncall: impact: connection queueing and a couple of OOM kills. Fast mitigation = revert values in canary (pin) + cap HPA to prevent replica storm.
maya: product wants to keep image changes (retry logic). So prefer pin->hotfix. Plan below, agree?
owen: agree. Steps: 1) helm hotpatch in canary to previous pool.max and idleTimeout, 2) patch HPA maxReplicas=4, 3) monitor DB conns & errors for 15m, 4) if stable -> record pin and promote; if not -> rollback images to v4.0.0.
release-ops: will open emergency change PR and a one-line audit note for the freeze window. Draft: "Canary: reverted db.pool values in eu-west due to unintended bump in chart v4.0.1; values pinned pending upstream chart fix. No customer-impact observed."
sre-oncall: applying suppression for noisy alerts for 15m and temporary 0% traffic split for canary if error rate > 1.5%.
maya: executing helm patch now: helm upgrade invoices-canary ./charts/invoices -n invoices-canary --reuse-values --set db.pool.max=60,db.pool.idleTimeout=60
(reported) helm upgrade succeeded. Pods rolling, one restart but back healthy. DB connections back to normal in ~2m.
owen: good. I'll open ticket for CI schema guard to reject pool.max > 200.
release-ops: PR: https://git.redwood/release-notes/PR-4555  tagging compliance.
sre-oncall: watching for 20m then final decision. Leaving thread open for rollback signal if any regression.
